metadata.title: Take Away Days (the Short)
metadata.role: trailer for The Birthday Paradox: Three Things You Could Change
metadata.note: audio is the clock; cues are on the Whisper word clock; not hand-edited

lines.title: THE BET
lines.narration_text: Twenty three people in a room. Bet me two of them share a birthday.
lines.on_screen: from the first frame: the headline "Two of these 23 share a day" and an empty calendar of 365 days (months down, days across), label "possible birthdays: 365". Dots start landing at 0.3 s, one every 0.25 s; the last two land in one cell, which is ringed.
lines.source_line: "Illustration: one random group of 23, seed 2701. Not data."

lines.title: HALF THE TIME
lines.narration_text: I'm Tanmay Kulkarni, for Humanitarians AI, and you'd lose that bet about half the time.
lines.on_screen: headline "You'd lose about half the time". As he says the name, a small name line fades in inside the safe area ("Tanmay Kulkarni · Humanitarians AI"). The counter fades in at 260 px: 50.7%, label "of random groups of 23 have a shared birthday".

lines.title: TAKE AWAY DAYS
lines.narration_text: Now keep the group at twenty three, and take away days. Squeeze the calendar to ninety days, and it's ninety five percent. Squeeze it to one month, and it's almost certain.
lines.on_screen: headline "Same 23 people. Fewer days." The calendar narrows around the same dots (a band of lit days shrinks from the full year to 90 days, then to 30; label "possible birthdays: 365 → 90 → 30" follows). The counter climbs with it: 95.4%, then "above 99.99%". Dots slide inward and pile onto shared days.

lines.title: WHAT DECIDES IT
lines.narration_text: So what decides it? Not the people, we kept them. Not uneven birthdays, they move it a tenth of a point. It's how many days there are.
lines.on_screen: headline "What decides it?" Three rows slide in below the narrowed calendar, one on each phrase: PEOPLE "23, kept"; EVENNESS "+0.1 point at most"; DAYS "365 → 30", ringed in the accent as the one that moved it.
lines.source_line: "Our calculation. Real US births, NCHS and SSA via FiveThirtyEight (CC BY 4.0)."

lines.title: THE RULE
lines.narration_text: Here's the rule. Take the square root of the days. Multiply by one point two. Add a half.
lines.on_screen: headline "The rule". The rows clear and the rule is typeset in three steps, each as it is spoken: √d, then 1.2 ×, then + ½ (final form: n ≈ round(1.2 × √d + ½), with d = possible birthdays, n = people for even odds, "even odds = a 50% chance").
lines.source_line: "Our calculation. Checked against the exact answer for every day count from 2 to 2,000."

lines.title: TRY IT
lines.narration_text: For even odds, a year needs twenty three people. One month needs seven.
lines.on_screen: headline "Try it". The calendar widens to a year: 23 dots, "365 days → 23 people for even odds". Then it narrows to a month: dots leave one by one until 7 remain, "30 days → 7 people for even odds".

lines.title: THAT'S WHY TWENTY THREE
lines.narration_text: That's why it's twenty three. The full video shows three things you could change, and the one that decides it. It's on Humanitarians AI.
lines.on_screen: the opening scene again, restored: a full year, 23 dots, the ringed pair, 50.7%. The rule fades. Closing text over the scene (inside the safe area, about 2.5 s): "The full video. Search:" then "The Birthday Paradox: Three Things You Could Change" then "Humanitarians AI". The exact title is searchable, so the pointer works even where a link cannot.
